classificationPolicy.static: Preserve major petrified stump/root/rock structure and ambiguous pale spires; static is a presentation decision, not an assertion of canonical invulnerability for every pebble.
classificationPolicy.mutable: Candidate standalone visual object requiring a complete backing surface; does not grant harvesting, movement, destruction, or simulation behavior.
classificationPolicy.effect: Existing visible motion/atmosphere candidate; gameplay liquid/light/visibility rules remain unimplemented.

geometryPolicy.estimateTolerancePixels: Approximately 6–16 pixels for readable small groups; substantially greater at intertwined structural boundaries.
geometryPolicy.candidatePolygon: Small colored-object polygons now bound the inspected complete plant envelope; color thresholding and connected-stem growth must derive final alpha inside them. Stone polygons have hand-adjusted 10–17 point outlines. Broad static partitions remain provisional.
geometryPolicy.overlap: Broad parent chunks intentionally overlap attached growth search regions. Resolve explicit front/back and keep each visible pixel owned once in the final reconstruction.
geometryPolicy.bounds: Some source regions touch image edges; clipped objects cannot become full standalone assets without separately marked reconstruction.
geometryPolicy.maskAcceptance: Trace/segment actual edges; retain thin stems and isolated caps; remove all checkerboard or backing contamination; inspect alpha and source-aligned recomposition.

backgroundOnly.policy: Retain tiny anonymous pebbles, sub-readable pale flecks, low moss, cobble grain and indistinct leaf speckle in backing ground. Do not multiply each fleck into an invented entity.
Dense vines, moss and small distant growth attached to the petrified wall remain structural texture except for separately listed readable groups. Requires close-scale audit before broader mutability.

gaps: Full left river-bank instance inventory, far-right cropped ecology and objects continuing below the frame are not complete. Edge ROIs are marked, not silently completed.
Backwall grain is continuous and roots interlock; chunk boundaries are compositing proposals, not inferred separable geological objects.
Small cream/ochre shapes may be fungi, mineral spires or weathered wood. Neutral visual labels are intentional; no species or item identification is supported.
Fine stems, tiny capped growth, vines and moss inside large root ROIs need per-pixel review. This full-frame audit cannot provide final segmentation.
The hidden floor/rock behind objects does not exist in the flattened source. Reconstructed backing must be labeled inferred, with material continuity checks and original-image recomposition QA.
Shadows are baked together with objects. A mutable object needs separated/reconstructed contact shadow handling so disappearance leaves neither a dark ghost nor a lighting seam.
Foot anchors are visual estimates. Existing layout collision/occlusion geometry remains authoritative as a proposal until a reviewed final manifest replaces it.
More than one visual object may exist within a grouped plant patch. Split only when source-scale inspection establishes independent silhouettes and supports.

The source-scale audit still leaves tiny shrubs/caps embedded in structural partitions; it does not certify one-to-one extraction of every background sprig. Static partitions and effects need separate full-silhouette review.
